symptom: `mxcli playwright check / /p/doesnotexist -p app.mpr` printed the home page's verdict for both (`title="Mendix - Homepage"  h="Welcome to your homepage"`) and `OK 2 page(s)`, exit 0 — a page URL that no page has passed the check
cause: The probe already captured the final location (finalUrl) but nothing compared it with the URL asked for, and nothing printed it. The runtime answers every /p/<x> with `301 Location: /#/<x>` whether or not a page has that URL; the client then replaces the location with /p/<x> for a known page and with / for an unknown one, rendering the home page plus an information dialog, with HTTP 200 throughout — so status, title, text and console were all clean
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck.go (ProbePages sets RequestedURL; landedAt/wrongPage; url= in formatPageVerdict; .mx-dialog-info in alerts), cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_assert.go (EvaluatePage)
insight: Measure the routing before choosing the signal: one curl (`curl -sD- /p/x` → 301 to /#/x, identical for known and unknown pages) and a 20ms poll of location.pathname in Playwright settled it on 11.13.0 and 11.15.0 in minutes — the client redirects (history.replaceState) rather than rendering in place, so the final path is a language-independent signal and needs no second load of the home page to compare titles. The not-found dialog ('The page you requested was not found. You are redirected to the home page.', .mx-dialog-info) is translated, so it is reported, not matched. Matching is exact: /p/ITEMS and /p/items/ also land on / on 11.13, so a case or trailing-slash typo now fails instead of silently checking the home page. Restrict the rule to /p/ requests: / and /#/x legitimately end elsewhere. The anonymous case (/login.html#/items) is the sign-in failure's, and must not also count as a wrong page. `run --page-check` gets the url= field for free because ProbePages sets RequestedURL; its verdict has no pass/fail
